signals.entity: ECB Banking Supervision (SSM significant institutions)
signals.country: Austria, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Greece, Slovakia, Slovenia (euro-area/SSM footprint)
signals.signal: ECB letter SSM-2026-0301 from Supervisory Board Chair Claudia Buch to CEOs of significant institutions, dated 07/07/2026, on AI-enabled cybersecurity threats. Banks must assess the impact of the evolving threat landscape 'without delay' and submit a comprehensive ACTION PLAN to their Joint Supervisory Team BY 31/10/2026. Short-term focus: accelerate vulnerability and patch management at scale; enhance monitoring/detection and AI-enabled defensive capabilities; verify ICT third-party risk management is fit for purpose. Structural measures: reinforce defence-in-depth and cyber hygiene, and MODERNISE INFRASTRUCTURE BY REPLACING OR UPDATING LEGACY, UNSUPPORTED OR END-OF-LIFE TECHNOLOGIES; improve response/recovery and crisis management. ECB will run a horizontal analysis of all action plans. As relief, ECB extends the annual IT Risk Questionnaire collection deadline from September 2026 to February 2027.
signals.source_name: ECB Banking Supervision — letter to CEOs of significant institutions, SSM-2026-0301 (PDF, text extracted locally)
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: every SSM significant institution in the footprint — Alpha/Piraeus/NBG/Eurobank (GR), Bank of Cyprus/Hellenic (CY), Erste/RBI/BAWAG/OeVAG (AT), Zagrebacka/PBZ/Erste HR, NLB/NKBM (SI), SlSp/VUB/Tatra (SK), UniCredit Bulbank/DSK/UBB (BG) — plus subsidiaries of Erste, RBI, UniCredit, OTP, NBG across the region. (b) BUY/CHANGE: the 'legacy, unsupported or end-of-life technologies' line lands directly on ATM and self-service estates still on unsupported OS/legacy multivendor stacks — Printec sells NCR Atleos ATM refresh (dispense/recycling/intelligent deposit), x-core multivendor ATM software to lift the fleet off end-of-life vendor stacks, ATM/device telemetry and monitoring for the 'enhance monitoring and detection' ask, INETCO transaction monitoring for anomaly detection on the payment rails, Thales HSM/PCI and remote key injection for perimeter/crypto hygiene, physical ATM security, and managed/field services (500+ engineers) to execute the estate refresh. Third-party-risk line also favours a single accountable managed-service partner over fragmented vendors. (c) BUDGET: action plans are due 31/10/2026 and will carry named timelines — vendor selection and capex sizing must happen Aug-Oct 2026, i.e. NOW, with delivery budget in the 2027 IT plan.
signals.likelihood: Very high — a dated, mandatory supervisory submission with horizontal ECB follow-up
signals.followup: Approach SSM significant institutions in GR/CY/AT/HR/SI/SK/BG in August-September 2026 with a 'legacy/end-of-life ICT remediation' pitch timed to the 31/10/2026 JST action-plan submission; ask which ATM/self-service assets are logged as end-of-life in their plan.

signals.entity: ESAs (EBA/EIOPA/ESMA) — critical ICT third-party providers (CTPPs)
signals.country: EU footprint: Austria, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Greece, Hungary, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia
signals.signal: On 18/11/2025 the three ESAs designated the FIRST list of critical ICT third-party providers under DORA Art.31 — 19 CTPPs, reported by press to include Amazon (AWS), Microsoft, Google, Oracle, SAP and Deutsche Telekom. Direct EU-level oversight of these 19 CTPPs STARTED IN JANUARY 2026 (confirmed by ECB Supervisory Board member Anneli Tuominen, 24/03/2026). The list will be updated and republished annually. Oversight fees are set by Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1505 of 22/02/2024: annual fee is turnover-based with a floor of EUR 50,000, and a fixed EUR 50,000 opt-in fee where a provider requests designation. Lead Overseer can levy periodic penalty payments up to 1% of the CTPP's average daily worldwide turnover, for up to six months.
signals.source_name: EBA press release 'The European Supervisory Authorities designate critical ICT third-party providers under DORA'; Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1505 (EUR-Lex); ECB/SSM Tuominen contribution 24/03/2026
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: every DORA-scope bank, payment institution and e-money institution in the 10 EU footprint countries that consumes cloud/platform services from the 19 designated CTPPs — which is effectively all of them. (b) BUY/CHANGE: CTPP designation does NOT remove the bank's own Art.28-30 obligations; banks must still evidence exit strategies, concentration limits and substitutability for cloud-hosted channels. This is the strongest current argument for on-prem/hybrid, vendor-diversified delivery of ATM channel software (x-core multivendor), device telemetry/monitoring, TMS for POS estates, and Thales HSMs where key material must not sit with a designated CTPP. (c) BUDGET: annual redesignation cycle means the next list lands ~Q4 2026; concentration-risk remediation programmes typically budget 6-12 months ahead, i.e. H2-2026 for 2027 delivery.
signals.likelihood: High — oversight is live and the list is refreshed annually
signals.followup: Obtain the ESAs' official CTPP list PDF from eba.europa.eu to confirm all 19 names (press-only at present); track the second annual designation round expected around Q4-2026.

signals.entity: ECB / SSM — ICT third-party risk and TLPT supervisory campaign
signals.country: Austria, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Greece, Slovakia, Slovenia (SSM) + spillover to CZ/HU/RO subsidiaries
signals.signal: ECB Supervisory Board member Anneli Tuominen, 24/03/2026: 38% of major ICT incidents reported by banks in 2025 had 'IT change' as root cause; cloud spend rose from ~4% of bank IT budgets in 2021 to 17% in 2025; the EU oversight framework for 19 CTPPs launched January 2026; banks LAG on contract renegotiations and business continuity planning. OVER 80 BANKING GROUPS have been notified for DORA threat-led penetration testing (TLPT) and the first three-year cycle is underway. ECB 2026-2028 supervisory priorities (published 18/11/2025) reduce to just TWO priorities, the second being 'strengthening banks' operational resilience and fostering robust ICT capabilities', with an ON-SITE CAMPAIGN on ICT third-party risk management planned.
signals.source_name: ECB Banking Supervision — 'Upgrading banks' capacity to deal with digital risks' (Tuominen); ECB Supervisory priorities 2026-28
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: 80+ notified banking groups EU-wide including the regional parents Erste, RBI, UniCredit, OTP, NBG, Alpha and their footprint subsidiaries. (b) BUY/CHANGE: 'IT change' as the top incident root cause is a direct argument for change-controlled, monitored device estates — Printec ATM/device telemetry and monitoring, x-core multivendor ATM software with controlled release management, TMS for POS terminal fleets (remote, auditable parameter and firmware change), and managed services with SLA-backed change windows. TLPT scoping pulls ATM/POS channels and HSM key management into red-team scope: Thales HSM/PCI, remote key injection, physical ATM security. (c) BUDGET: TLPT cycles run 6-12 months per test and qualified red-team providers are booking far ahead — remediation capex for notified groups needs committing in 2026-2027.
signals.likelihood: High — on-site campaign is a stated 2026-28 supervisory priority
signals.followup: Ask footprint SSM banks whether they are among the 80+ TLPT-notified groups and whether ATM/POS channels are in TLPT scope; pitch telemetry + change-control as the 'IT change root cause' remedy.

signals.entity: FMA Austria / Oesterreichische Nationalbank (OeNB)
signals.signal: [NEW] FMA and OeNB joint one-year DORA review published 16/01/2026: Austrian financial entities filed 103 notifications of MAJOR ICT incidents to the FMA in 2025, and approximately 63% of those incidents INVOLVED EXTERNAL ICT SERVICE PROVIDERS. The OeNB TIBER Cyber Team has identified the entities obliged to run threat-led penetration testing and has completed a preparatory pilot phase; systemically important Austrian financial firms must run a TLPT every three years. FMA/OeNB sit on the joint oversight teams for the 19 EU CTPPs. Separately, FMA set the 2026 annual Register of Information submission window as 16/02/2026-13/03/2026 via the FMA Incoming Platform, reference date 31/12/2025.
signals.source_name: OeNB press release 'Cybersicherheit gestärkt: FMA und OeNB ziehen positive Bilanz nach einem Jahr DORA' [Cybersecurity strengthened: FMA and OeNB draw a positive balance after one year of DORA]; FMA DORA-Dialog Informationsregister
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: all Austrian banks and payment/e-money institutions — Erste Group, RBI, BAWAG, Volksbanken, Bank Austria, plus their CEE subsidiary networks which inherit group ICT standards. (b) BUY/CHANGE: 63% of major incidents traced to external ICT providers makes vendor-side resilience a purchasing criterion — Printec must lead with DORA-ready contractual terms (Art.30 clauses, audit rights, exit plan, subcontracting transparency), monitored/managed service SLAs, and device telemetry that gives the bank its own incident evidence rather than depending on the vendor's word. TIBER-AT/TLPT scoping creates demand for hardened ATM software, HSM key management and physical ATM security. (c) BUDGET: the 2027 RoI window opens ~Feb-2027; TLPT engagements booked 12-18 months ahead means Austrian groups commit budget in H2-2026.
signals.likelihood: High
signals.followup: Use the 63%-third-party-incident statistic in Austrian and Austrian-parented (Erste/RBI) tenders as the case for a single accountable managed-service provider with DORA-compliant contract terms.

signals.entity: National competent authorities — DORA Register of Information annual cycle
signals.country: Austria, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Greece, Hungary, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia
signals.signal: The Register of Information (RoI — the mandatory register of every contractual arrangement for ICT services with third-party providers, format set by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2956) moved in 2026 from a one-off 2025 dry run to a hard ANNUAL cycle. NCAs must forward consolidated registers to the ESAs by 31 MARCH each year, reference date 31 December of the prior year, so national deadlines fall earlier. Confirmed 2026 national windows in the footprint: AUSTRIA (FMA) 16/02/2026-13/03/2026; CZECHIA (CNB) submission by 02/03/2026; SLOVAKIA (NBS) request issued to entities during February 2026, submission via IS SZP-ESAs in EBA reporting framework 4.0; BULGARIA (FSC/KFN, notice dated 05/03/2026) entities to file by 23/03/2026, ESAs production environment opened 25/02/2026, hard stop 31/03/2026, corrections resubmitted by 30/04/2026; CYPRUS (CySEC Circular C751, 19/01/2026) RoI due annually by 28 FEBRUARY.
signals.source_name: Bulgarian FSC (KFN) notice 'Срок за предоставяне на информационния регистър съгласно DORA' [Deadline for providing the information register under DORA]; FMA Austria DORA-Dialog; CNB DORA/SDAT page; NBS Slovakia Register informácií page; CySEC Circular C751
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: every DORA-scope credit institution, payment institution, e-money institution, investment firm and crypto-asset service provider in the 10 EU footprint states. (b) BUY/CHANGE: the RoI forces banks to enumerate, at contract and subcontract level, every ICT service supporting a critical or important function — including ATM managed services, ATM/POS software, terminal management, HSM services, cash-management software and document management. Printec must supply, as standard sales collateral, its own RoI data pack (LEI, entity hierarchy, subcontractor chain, country of data processing, substitutability assessment) or lose deals on procurement hygiene alone. This is also a lead-generation asset: a bank that cannot map its ATM estate's ICT dependencies is a candidate for a telemetry/monitoring and managed-service consolidation. (c) BUDGET: the next reference date is 31/12/2026 with national filings Feb-Mar 2027 — contract remediation must be underway by Q4-2026.
signals.likelihood: Certain — recurring statutory annual obligation
signals.followup: Build a reusable Printec DORA RoI/Art.30 contract annex; verify each footprint NCA's 2027 window when published (Q4-2026/Q1-2027).

signals.entity: Bank of Albania (Banka e Shqipërisë)
signals.signal: [NEW — non-EU DORA mirror] At its meeting of 01/07/2026 the Supervisory Council of the Bank of Albania ADOPTED the Regulation on 'Digital Operational Resilience' and approved amendments to the Regulation on 'Use of Information and Communication Technology by entities licensed by the Bank of Albania'. The BoA states this is part of aligning its supervisory framework with the EU acquis under Albania's EU integration commitments — i.e. a national DORA mirror. Albanian press reporting (Javanews, 10/07/2026) describes the regime as covering banks, payment institutions, e-money institutions, account information service providers, asset-token issuers and third-party ICT providers, with major-incident initial notification no later than FOUR HOURS from classification as major (or 24 hours from discovery), intermediate report within 72 hours, final report within one month; annual testing of systems supporting critical functions for all but micro-entities; and TLPT every three years for designated institutions. NOTE: the entry-into-force date is NOT confirmed by a primary source — one press outlet reports 15 days after Official Gazette publication, another reports 01/07/2027; treat as unverified.
signals.source_name: Bank of Albania press release 'Decisions by the Supervisory Council, 1 July 2026' (primary, fetched with desktop UA); Javanews.al [New rules for banks: cyber attacks to be reported within 4 hours, mandatory annual testing] (press)
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: all 11 banks in Albania (incl. Printec reference customers OTP Bank Albania and Raiffeisen Bank Albania), plus payment/e-money institutions and — importantly — THIRD-PARTY ICT PROVIDERS serving them, which brings Printec Albania itself into scope as a supplier that must meet contractual, audit and incident-cooperation obligations. (b) BUY/CHANGE: a 4-hour major-incident clock is unachievable without automated detection on the channel estate — Printec ATM/device telemetry and monitoring, INETCO transaction monitoring for real-time payment-flow anomaly detection, and 24x7 managed service/NOC coverage. Annual resilience testing plus 3-yearly TLPT drives spend on hardened ATM software (x-core), Thales HSM/remote key injection and physical ATM security. (c) BUDGET: Albanian banks must budget in the FY2027 IT plan — i.e. decisions in Q4-2026 — with a longer runway if the 01/07/2027 date is correct.
signals.likelihood: High — regulation formally adopted by the Supervisory Council
signals.followup: Obtain the adopted regulation text and its Fletorja Zyrtare (Official Gazette) publication number/date from bankofalbania.org to fix the entry-into-force date and any transitional period; then brief OTP Albania and Raiffeisen Albania. Flag Printec's own in-scope status as an ICT third-party provider to Printec Compliance.

signals.entity: National Bank of Ukraine (NBU)
signals.signal: [NEW] NBU Board Resolution No.143 of 09/12/2025, 'On Approval of the Regulation on the organisation of information security and cyber protection measures by financial service providers', entered into force 13/12/2025 and gives NON-BANK financial service providers (insurers, credit unions, finance companies, pawnshops) TWELVE MONTHS — to 13/12/2026 — to comply in full. Requirements include a named information-security officer, board-approved internal policies, asset inventory, access control with multi-factor authentication for remote access, minimum password lengths (12 characters users / 15 privileged), lockout after 5 failed attempts, 15-minute session lock, network segmentation with firewalls, vendor-supported operating systems only, event logging with at least one year retention, and a documented cyber/IS incident management process. For BANKS, the equivalent framework is NBU Resolution No.178 of 12/08/2022 (organisation of cyber protection in the banking system) and Resolution No.4 of 16/01/2021 (supervision of banks' IS/cyber/trust-services compliance), both amended by NBU Board Resolution No.24 of 25/02/2025 (officially published 28/02/2025, in force the following day).
signals.source_name: NBU Resolution No.143 on zakon.rada.gov.ua (official legal portal); NBU Resolution No.24 of 25/02/2025 PDF on bank.gov.ua (403 to fetch tool, retrieved with desktop User-Agent and text-extracted locally)
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: Ukrainian non-bank financial service providers face a hard 13/12/2026 compliance date; Ukrainian banks (incl. Printec reference customer PrivatBank) operate under the amended Resolutions 178/2022 and 4/2021. (b) BUY/CHANGE: 'operating systems requiring vendor security support' explicitly outlaws end-of-life OS — a direct trigger for ATM/self-service OS refresh and for x-core multivendor ATM software; MFA for remote access and network segmentation drive secure remote-management architecture for ATM/POS estates; one-year event-log retention and documented incident management drive telemetry/monitoring and INETCO transaction monitoring; Thales HSM/remote key injection for cryptographic controls. (c) BUDGET: with a 13/12/2026 hard stop for non-banks, procurement must close by roughly Q3-2026 — this is immediate.
signals.likelihood: High — hard statutory deadline inside 6 months
signals.followup: Map which Ukrainian non-bank FIs Printec already serves (POS/acquiring, terminal management) and pitch an OS-support + logging + MFA remediation bundle before Q4-2026. Confirm whether NBU has signalled a bank-facing DORA-equivalent operational-resilience regulation as part of EU accession screening Cluster 2.

signals.entity: Republic of Serbia — Law on Information Security / National Bank of Serbia
signals.signal: [NEW — non-EU NIS2 mirror] Serbia's new Law on Information Security was published in Sluzbeni glasnik RS no. 91/2025 and entered into force on 31/10/2025, transposing EU Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2) as part of EU accession alignment. Banks and payment service providers are classified as operators of PRIORITY ICT systems of special importance: annual (minimum) risk assessment, incident notification within 24 HOURS of discovering a significant incident, compliance checks twice yearly, and severity-based incident categorisation. The Government must issue implementing regulations defining operator categorisation criteria within one year of entry into force, i.e. BY 31/10/2026. Fines: up to RSD 2,000,000 (~EUR 17,000) for priority operators, up to RSD 1,000,000 (~EUR 8,500) for important operators. This sits alongside the NBS's existing decision on minimum standards for management of financial institutions' information systems and NBS incident-reporting requirements.
signals.source_name: Zunic Law analysis of Zakon o informacionoj bezbednosti, Sluzbeni glasnik RS 91/2025 (press/law-firm; primary gazette citation given)
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: all Serbian banks (incl. Printec reference customers Raiffeisen Banka Srbija and AIK Banka) and payment service providers. (b) BUY/CHANGE: a 24-hour incident clock plus twice-yearly compliance checks requires automated detection and auditable evidence across the channel estate — Printec ATM/device telemetry and monitoring, INETCO transaction monitoring, managed services with documented incident runbooks; annual risk assessment drives penetration/resilience testing on ATM and POS estates; x-core multivendor ATM software for controlled, evidenced change management. (c) BUDGET: implementing regulations are due by 31/10/2026 and will set the categorisation and control detail — Serbian banks should be sizing budget in H2-2026 for 2027.
signals.likelihood: High for the law; Medium for the implementing-regulation date holding
signals.followup: VERIFY against the primary text in Sluzbeni glasnik RS 91/2025 and against the NBS's own propisi page (nbs.rs) — this row currently rests on a law-firm summary. Also check whether the NBS has issued or consulted on a DORA-mirroring decision for banks specifically.

signals.entity: European Commission — Digital Omnibus and Cybersecurity Package (NIS2 / DORA incident reporting)
signals.country: All 10 EU footprint states (and indirectly the 7 non-EU via accession alignment)
signals.signal: [NEW] Two Commission files now sit over DORA incident reporting. (1) The Digital Omnibus package proposes a SINGLE ENTRY POINT (SEP) for cyber-incident reporting, to be built and operated by ENISA, so that one notification satisfies NIS2, DORA, GDPR, CER, eIDAS and the Cyber Resilience Act — 'report once, share many'. Use of the SEP would apply 18 months after entry into force of the measures, extendable to 24 months if the Commission judges the platform not yet fit on integrity/reliability/confidentiality. The mechanics are delivered mainly by amending the NIS2 Directive, with consequential amendments to DORA. (2) On 20/01/2026 the Commission proposed a Cybersecurity Package: a 'Cybersecurity Act 2' Regulation replacing Regulation (EU) 2019/881, plus a Directive amending NIS2 — clarifying scope and definitions, adding a small mid-cap category, and creating an ICT supply-chain security framework. Adoption is not expected before late 2026/early 2027, so no application date is fixed.
signals.source_name: European Commission, Shaping Europe's Digital Future — 'Proposal for a Directive as regards simplification measures and alignment with the Cybersecurity Act'; corroborated by Bird & Bird, Hunton, Freshfields, Clifford Chance analyses
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: all DORA-scope entities in the 10 EU footprint states; the ICT supply-chain security framework would also reach ICT vendors such as Printec directly. (b) BUY/CHANGE: no immediate spend, but it changes the target architecture — banks building DORA incident-reporting tooling now should not hard-wire to national portals. For Printec the ICT supply-chain security strand is the material item: expect customers to demand supply-chain attestations, SBOM-style transparency and subcontractor disclosure on ATM/POS software and managed services. (c) BUDGET: watch, do not spend; realistic application 2028-2029.
signals.likelihood: Medium — proposals only, co-legislators not yet agreed
signals.followup: Track the EP/Council files through H2-2026; prepare a Printec supply-chain security attestation pack in anticipation of customer due-diligence questions.

signals.entity: European Commission / CJEU — NIS2 transposition infringements
signals.country: EU-wide; footprint countries NOT among those referred
signals.signal: [NEW] On 08/07/2026 the European Commission referred IRELAND, SPAIN, FRANCE and the NETHERLANDS to the Court of Justice of the EU for failing to notify complete transposition of the NIS2 Directive, requesting financial sanctions (lump sum plus daily penalties until notification). The procedure ran from letters of formal notice on 28/11/2024 (23 Member States opened) and reasoned opinions on 07/05/2025. NO footprint jurisdiction is in the referral batch, which implies the 10 EU footprint states have at least notified transposition — but that is an inference, not a Commission statement, and per-country status still needs confirming.
signals.source_name: INSIGHT EU Monitoring / TechTimes reporting of the Commission's July 2026 infringement package (press — primary Commission infringement decision page not yet opened)
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: indirectly, banks in footprint states where national NIS2 laws are already in force and now being enforced. (b) BUY/CHANGE: national NIS2 regimes typically require management-body accountability, incident notification and supply-chain security for banks that are also 'essential entities' — reinforcing the same telemetry/monitoring, incident-detection and vendor-attestation spend as DORA. (c) BUDGET: national, varies.
signals.likelihood: High for the referral fact; Medium for the footprint inference
signals.followup: Open the Commission's July 2026 infringement decisions register (ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner INF/26/...) to confirm the exact list and check whether any footprint state is at reasoned-opinion stage for INCOMPLETE (as opposed to non-) transposition.

signals.entity: DORA threat-led penetration testing (TLPT) — RTS and TIBER-EU national adoption
signals.country: Adopted TIBER: Austria, Czech Republic, Romania, Slovakia. NOT adopted: Greece, Croatia, Hungary, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Slovenia
signals.signal: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1190 — the RTS on threat-led penetration testing under DORA Art.26(11) — was published in the Official Journal on 18/06/2025 and applies from 08/07/2025. It sets the criteria identifying which financial entities must run TLPT, the scope and methodology, requirements for internal testers, and rules for supervisory cooperation and mutual recognition of tests. TLPT must be performed at least every three years. The ECB's TIBER-EU framework (published May-2018) was updated in 2024 to align fully with the TLPT RTS; the ECB lists adoption in 20 jurisdictions including four footprint countries — Austria, Czechia, Romania (TIBER-RO, established by NBR Regulation no.6/2022) and Slovakia — while Greece, Croatia, Hungary, Bulgaria, Cyprus and Slovenia are NOT listed as TIBER adopters, meaning their entities run TLPT under the RTS via their NCA or, for significant institutions, the ECB.
signals.source_name: ECB 'What is TIBER-EU?' (adoption list); Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1190, OJ 18/06/2025
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: designated systemically important banks in all 10 EU footprint states; 80+ EU banking groups already notified per the ECB (24/03/2026), with further national notifications expected late-2026/early-2027. (b) BUY/CHANGE: TLPT red-teams routinely target the physical/self-service channel — ATM network segmentation, ATM OS hardening, remote-management paths, HSM key handling and card-data flows. Findings convert into spend on x-core multivendor ATM software, ATM/device telemetry, Thales HSM/PCI and remote key injection, physical ATM security, and INETCO transaction monitoring for detection coverage. (c) BUDGET: red-team capacity in the EU is scarce and booked far ahead; banks must commit test and remediation budget 6-12 months before their slot.
signals.likelihood: High
signals.followup: Confirm whether Greece (BoG), Croatia (HNB), Hungary (MNB), Bulgaria (BNB), Cyprus (CBC) or Slovenia (BS) have since stood up national TIBER frameworks — the ECB page may lag. Position Printec as the remediation partner post-TLPT rather than as the tester.

signals.entity: Bank of Greece — DORA incident reporting
signals.signal: The Bank of Greece maintains a dedicated DORA page ('DORA — Ψηφιακή Επιχειρησιακή Ανθεκτικότητα Χρηματοοικονομικού Τομέα' [DORA — Digital Operational Resilience of the Financial Sector]) setting out the four obligation pillars (ICT risk management; incident management, classification and reporting; digital operational resilience testing — annual minimum with TLPT every three years; ICT third-party risk management). The page carries reporting templates dated JUNE 2026 for 'Αναφορά Μείζονος Συμβάντος ΤΠΕ' [Major ICT Incident Report] and 'Αναφορά Σημαντικών Κυβερνοαπειλών' [Significant Cyber Threats Report], filed to ICTIncidentReporting@bankofgreece.gr. Registers of information follow Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2956. No Bank of Greece Executive Committee Act (ΠΕΕ) specific to DORA is published on that page.
signals.source_name: Bank of Greece — DORA page (Greek)
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: Greek significant institutions (NBG, Piraeus, Alpha, Eurobank — Alpha is a Printec Siron AML reference), less significant institutions, payment and e-money institutions. (b) BUY/CHANGE: email-based major-incident reporting with refreshed June-2026 templates means the binding constraint is DETECTION and evidence, not filing — Printec ATM/device telemetry, INETCO transaction monitoring and managed-service NOC coverage supply the timestamps and impact data the template demands. Annual resilience testing of critical-function systems pulls the ATM/POS estate into scope. (c) BUDGET: continuous obligation; align with the Greek banks' 2027 IT plans set in Q4-2026.
signals.likelihood: High
signals.followup: Download the June-2026 BoG incident templates to see exactly which technical fields (affected channels, transaction volumes, downtime) banks must produce, and map them to Printec telemetry outputs as a sales asset.

signals.entity: Magyar Nemzeti Bank (MNB)
signals.signal: MNB operates a certificate-based DORA Register of Information reporting channel inside its ERA system ('DORA szolgáltatói nyilvántartás'), with a published user manual (DORA ROI Felhasználói kézikönyv). Registration for the reporting interface opened 01/04/2025 with full availability from 07/04/2025; submission is at INDIVIDUAL entity level except for Hungarian-headquartered credit institutions that are EU-level parent undertakings, which report at consolidated level. MNB has published Hungarian-language notices on the DORA RoI ITS, the incident-reporting RTS/ITS, and the ESAs' CTPP designation data-collection timetable. Specific 2026 Hungarian filing dates are set by individual MNB orders (végzés) to each entity rather than a single public deadline.
signals.source_name: MNB supervisory news 'Tájékoztatás a DORA szerinti IKT-szolgáltatások igénybevételéről szóló információ-nyilvántartás adatszolgáltatási felületre való regisztráció megkezdéséről' [Notice on the opening of registration for the DORA ICT-services information-register reporting interface]; MNB DORA ROI user manual (era.mnb.hu)
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: OTP Bank, MBH Bank, K&H, Erste Hungary, Raiffeisen Hungary, UniCredit Hungary and Hungarian payment/e-money institutions. (b) BUY/CHANGE: entity-level RoI filing across a group like OTP (which runs subsidiaries in 8 footprint markets) multiplies the contract-data burden — Printec should supply a group-ready RoI annex covering every Printec entity, subcontractor and country of processing. (c) BUDGET: continuous; the 2027 cycle lands Q1-2027.
signals.likelihood: High
signals.followup: Confirm MNB's 2026 filing window (issued by individual végzés, not published centrally) via a Hungarian customer; separately check MNB's NIS2/IT-audit expectations, historically a Hungarian over-implementation and a fast spend trigger.

signals.entity: Central Bank of Montenegro (CBCG) / Government of Montenegro
signals.signal: [NEW — non-EU DORA mirror, now LAW not draft] The CBCG Council at its session of 28/11/2025 adopted the Draft Law on Digital Operational Resilience of the Financial Sector (Nacrt zakona o digitalnoj operativnoj otpornosti finansijskog sektora), one of three draft laws CBCG described as key to closing EU accession Chapter 9 (Financial Services). The law has since been enacted and is listed on the CBCG's own 'Zakoni' regulatory page as 'Zakon o digitalnoj operativnoj otpornosti finansijskog sektora', Sluzbeni list Crne Gore br. 14/26 (2026). Critically, CBCG states the law's APPLICATION BEGINS ON THE DAY MONTENEGRO ACCEDES TO THE EU — i.e. it is on the statute book now but dormant, giving Montenegrin banks a defined but open-ended runway. The two companion drafts amend the Law on Financial Conglomerates (aligning with Directive (EU) 2023/2864) and the Law on Financial Collateral.
signals.source_name: CBCG — Zakoni (regulatory register, cbcg.me) listing Zakon o digitalnoj operativnoj otpornosti finansijskog sektora, Sl. list CG 14/26; Portal Analitika 'Utvrdjeni nacrti tri zakona kljucna za zatvaranje poglavlja 9' [Three draft laws key to closing Chapter 9 adopted] (press corroboration of the 28/11/2025 Council session)
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: all 11 Montenegrin banks (the same 11 that went live on the Western Balkans TIPS clone on 20/07/2026 under CBCG), plus payment and e-money institutions and, by DORA's design, their ICT third-party providers — which brings Printec Montenegro into scope as a supplier. (b) BUY/CHANGE: a DORA-equivalent regime imports ICT risk management, major-incident classification and reporting, annual resilience testing of systems supporting critical functions, TLPT for designated entities, and a register of information on every ICT contract. On the channel estate that means ATM/device telemetry and monitoring for detection and evidence, x-core multivendor ATM software for controlled and auditable change management, INETCO transaction monitoring on the new instant-payment rails, Thales HSM/PCI and remote key injection, and managed services with contractual DORA Article 30-style terms. (c) BUDGET: because application is tied to EU accession, there is NO hard near-term spend date — treat this as a design constraint on 2027-2028 ATM/POS refresh and instant-payment projects rather than a compliance deadline, and use it to sell DORA-ready contract terms today so systems bought now are not re-procured later.
signals.likelihood: Certain that the law exists; timing of application is entirely contingent on EU accession
signals.followup: Retrieve the full text of Sl. list CG 14/26 to confirm the exact publication date, whether any provisions (e.g. incident reporting to CBCG) apply BEFORE accession, and whether CBCG has separately issued or plans a subordinate decision on ICT risk that binds banks in the interim. Note that the CBCG's existing decision on information-system management remains the operative rule until then.

signals.entity: SZTFH (Szabalyozott Tevekenysegek Felugyeleti Hatosaga) — Hungarian cybersecurity supervisor
signals.signal: [NEW] Hungary's mandatory NIS2 CYBERSECURITY AUDIT deadline CLOSED on 30/06/2026. SZTFH announced on 10/07/2026 that of 2,520 registered audit-obligated organisations, 2,132 (84.6%) met the deadline; 1,511 audit reports had been processed and 170 organisations were rated 'negligible risk'. Organisations that missed it face enforcement: warnings and fines UP TO HUF 150 MILLION (approx. EUR 380,000-500,000 depending on rate). Predecessor milestones: entities registered before 01/01/2025 had to contract an auditor by 31/08/2025 and complete the audit by 30/06/2026; entities in supervised high-risk sectors had to complete audits by 31/12/2025. The audit procedure and its capped fee are set by a dedicated SZTFH rendelet (decree). SZTFH states cybersecurity is a continuing capability, not a one-off state — a recurring audit cycle follows.
signals.source_name: SZTFH — 'Lezarult a kiberbiztonsagi auditok hatarideje' [The cybersecurity audit deadline has closed]; SZTFH 'NIS2 — Megjelent a kiberbiztonsagi audit eljarasrendjerol es maximalizalt dijarol szolo SZTFH rendelet' [SZTFH decree on the cybersecurity audit procedure and capped fee published]
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: Hungarian entities in NIS2 scope — for banking, OTP Bank, MBH Bank, K&H, Erste Hungary, Raiffeisen Hungary, UniCredit Hungary and their ICT suppliers. Banks are dually regulated: DORA for financial ICT risk (MNB) and the NIS2 regime for the general cybersecurity/audit duty (SZTFH). This is exactly the Hungarian over-implementation pattern the Printec playbook flags as a fast spend trigger — an EXTERNAL AUDITOR now signs off on the control environment. (b) BUY/CHANGE: audit findings are the purchase order. Recurring third-party audit of asset inventory, network segmentation, logging, patching and supplier management lands directly on the ATM/self-service and POS estates — ATM/device telemetry and monitoring (evidence and log retention), x-core multivendor ATM software to retire unsupported vendor stacks flagged by auditors, TMS for auditable POS firmware/parameter change, Thales HSM and remote key injection for key-management findings, physical ATM security, and managed/field services to execute remediation. (c) BUDGET: 388 organisations are already in breach as of 10/07/2026 and remediation from the completed audits runs through H2-2026; the next cycle's auditor contracting will again land ~12 months ahead. Hungarian remediation budget commits NOW for 2027 delivery.
signals.likelihood: Very high — deadline has passed and SZTFH has published enforcement intent with a stated fine ceiling
signals.followup: Ask Hungarian customers (OTP group especially, which exports its standards to 8 footprint subsidiaries) for the ICT-infrastructure findings in their 2026 cybersecurity audit report and offer a remediation package. Confirm the exact SZTFH decree number and the statutory periodicity of the audit cycle from the Magyar Kozlony text before quoting the next deadline.

signals.entity: Republic of Bulgaria — Law on Cybersecurity (Zakon za kibersigurnost), NIS2 transposition
signals.signal: [NEW] Bulgaria's amended Law on Cybersecurity, transposing Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2), was PROMULGATED IN DARJAVEN VESTNIK (State Gazette) issue 17 of 13/02/2026, updating the 2018 Cybersecurity Act. It widens scope from 6 to 18 sectors, introduces the essential/important entity split with proportionate minimum security measures, management-body accountability and a strict staged incident-notification regime. Bulgaria was, until this act, one of the last footprint states without complete NIS2 transposition (the Commission opened letters of formal notice against 23 Member States on 28/11/2024 and issued reasoned opinions on 07/05/2025; the 08/07/2026 CJEU referral batch named Ireland, Spain, France and the Netherlands — no footprint state). Bulgarian banks are simultaneously in DORA scope (BNB/FSC) and, from 01/01/2026, in the euro area and therefore SSM/ECB-supervised for the significant institutions.
signals.source_name: Capital.bg 'Promenite v Zakona za kibersigurnost i zadalzheniyata za biznesa' [The changes to the Cybersecurity Act and business obligations] citing Darjaven vestnik br.17/13.02.2026 (press; primary DV text not opened)
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: Bulgarian banks (UniCredit Bulbank, DSK, UBB, Postbank, Fibank) and payment/e-money institutions, plus their ICT suppliers. Note DORA is lex specialis for financial entities' ICT risk, so the practical NIS2 bite for banks is on supply-chain security duties and on their non-financial ICT vendors. (b) BUY/CHANGE: supply-chain security obligations mean Bulgarian banks will push attestations, subcontractor disclosure and incident-cooperation clauses down to ATM/POS software and managed-service vendors — Printec must be able to answer these to stay on panel. Detection and staged notification again favour telemetry/monitoring and INETCO. (c) BUDGET: this stacks on top of the euro-changeover ATM/POS programme Bulgarian banks executed for 01/01/2026 — the 2027 IT plan set in Q4-2026 is the window.
signals.likelihood: High for the law; Medium on how hard it bites banks given DORA lex specialis
signals.followup: VERIFY against the primary Darjaven vestnik br.17/2026 text on dv.parliament.bg and check the BNB's own site for any accompanying banking-sector guidance; this row currently rests on Bulgarian press. Confirm the fine ceilings and the entity-registration deadline set by the act.

signals.entity: Hrvatska narodna banka (HNB) — Croatian DORA implementation
signals.signal: [NEW detail] Croatia implements DORA through a dedicated national act: Zakon o provedbi Uredbe (EU) 2022/2554 o digitalnoj operativnoj otpornosti za financijski sektor, Narodne novine br. 136/2024. Under its Article 8(3) HNB is the competent authority for credit institutions, payment institutions, account information service providers, e-money institutions and asset-referenced token issuers; Article 14 requires reporting of major ICT incidents to BOTH HNB and the National CERT; Article 15 mandates that reporting go through the national cyber threat/incident platform PiXi (https://pixi.carnet.hr/, run by CARNET, accessed via the NIAS national eID), and Article 19 sets the offence/penalty provisions for failing to report. HNB published implementing 'Smjernice za izvjescivanje HNB-a o znacajnim IKT incidentima i ozbiljnim kiberneticim prijetnjama putem Platforme PiXi' [Guidelines on reporting major ICT incidents and serious cyber threats to HNB via the PiXi platform] in JULY 2025, applying Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1772 (incident classification criteria and materiality thresholds) and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/301 of 23/10/2024 (content and TIME LIMITS for the initial notification, intermediate report and final report). DORA's start also SWEPT AWAY the previous Croatian ICT incident-reporting regimes under the Odluka o primjerenom upravljanju informacijskim sustavom (NN 110/2022, 152/2024), the Payment System Act and EBA/GL/2021/03 PSD2 incident guidelines. Serious cyber threats may be reported voluntarily via PiXi.
signals.source_name: HNB — Smjernice za izvjescivanje HNB-a o znacajnim IKT incidentima ... putem Platforme PiXi (PDF, July 2025, text extracted locally); Zakon o provedbi Uredbe (EU) 2022/2554, NN 136/2024
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: Zagrebacka banka, PBZ, Erste&Steiermarkische (a Printec OptiCash reference), OTP Croatia, RBA Croatia, HPB, plus Croatian payment and e-money institutions. (b) BUY/CHANGE: the binding constraint is DETECTION AND EVIDENCE within the 2025/301 clock, not the filing channel — a bank cannot file an initial notification it has not detected. ATM/device telemetry and monitoring, INETCO transaction monitoring on the payment rails and 24x7 managed-service NOC coverage supply the timestamps, affected-channel counts and downtime figures the templates demand; x-core multivendor ATM software gives auditable change control (recall ECB's finding that 38% of 2025 major ICT incidents were caused by IT change). Penalty exposure under Article 19 makes this a board-level topic. (c) BUDGET: standing obligation; align with Croatian banks' 2027 IT plans set Q4-2026, and with the annual Register of Information cycle.
signals.likelihood: Certain — in force and operational
signals.followup: Extract the exact initial/intermediate/final report deadlines from Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/301 and build a one-page 'can your ATM estate meet this clock?' asset for Croatian banks. Confirm HNB's 2026 Register of Information submission window from hnb.hr.

signals.entity: European Commission / ESAs — DORA ICT subcontracting RTS
signals.country: All 10 EU footprint states (Austria, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Greece, Hungary, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia)
signals.signal: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/532 of 24/03/2025, the RTS specifying what a financial entity must determine and assess when SUBCONTRACTING ICT services that support critical or important functions, was published in the Official Journal on 02/07/2025 and entered into force on the twentieth day following publication (22/07/2025). It requires financial entities to assess the LENGTH AND COMPLEXITY OF THE SUBCONTRACTING CHAIN and whether services are CONCENTRATED IN A SINGLE SUBCONTRACTOR; to perform due diligence that the ICT provider can itself select and assess the operational and financial capability of its subcontractors; to specify contractually which services may be subcontracted; to require the provider to monitor all subcontracted ICT services so its own obligations remain met; to be notified of intended material changes with a reasonable notice period in which to approve or object; and to hold termination rights where the provider changes or subcontracts without approval. This is the missing piece behind the annual Register of Information, which must be populated at subcontract level.
signals.source_name: EUR-Lex — Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/532, CELEX 32025R0532, OJ 02/07/2025
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: every DORA-scope bank, payment institution, e-money institution and investment firm in the 10 EU footprint states — and, contractually, every ICT vendor to them including Printec. (b) BUY/CHANGE: this is the single most commercially material DORA text for Printec because it regulates PRINTEC'S OWN supply chain. Printec must be able to hand a bank, as standard tender collateral, a full subcontractor map for every service line (NCR Atleos for ATM hardware/software, Glory/Sesami for recyclers, Verifone/Castles for POS, Thales for HSM, Namirial for eKYC, IMTF/FICO/INETCO for AML and monitoring, plus field-service subcontractors), with country of processing, substitutability assessment, change-notification commitments and termination rights. Vendors that cannot are removed at procurement. Conversely it is a wedge: a bank running a fragmented multi-vendor ATM/POS estate faces a longer, more complex subcontracting chain than one consolidated with a single accountable managed-service partner — that is the Printec managed-services pitch, stated in the regulator's own language. (c) BUDGET: in force since 22/07/2025; contract remediation is being done through the 2026-2027 Register of Information cycles, so the commercial deadline is CONTINUOUS and every renewal is a checkpoint.
signals.likelihood: Certain — in force
signals.followup: Commission Printec Legal/Compliance to produce a reusable DORA Article 30 + 2025/532 contract annex and subcontractor register pack per product line, and make it a standard tender attachment across the 10 EU footprint markets. Flag to Printec Compliance that Printec is itself a regulated-by-contract ICT third-party provider in Albania and (on accession) Montenegro.

signals.entity: ESAs (EBA/EIOPA/ESMA) — Joint Oversight Venture and Joint Examination Teams
signals.signal: [NEW] Operational EU-level oversight of the 19 designated critical ICT third-party providers (CTPPs) STARTED IN 2026. The three ESAs have set up a JOINT OVERSIGHT VENTURE (JOV) led by a Joint Oversight Director to concentrate resources and ensure consistency, and oversight is executed by JOINT EXAMINATION TEAMS (JETs) staffed by ESA personnel, the national competent authorities supervising the financial entities that use the CTPP, and the NIS authorities supervising the CTPP itself. JETs can request information, conduct ongoing monitoring, run investigations and on-site inspections, and issue recommendations directly to a CTPP; where a CTPP does not comply, the Lead Overseer can require financial entities to suspend or terminate use of its services. The ESAs also consulted on technical standards governing JET composition and functioning. NCAs from the footprint (FMA/OeNB, BNB, HNB, CBC, CNB, BoG, MNB, BNR, NBS-SK, Banka Slovenije) sit on these teams.
signals.source_name: EIOPA — 'DORA oversight' page (esas joint oversight framework); ESMA press release 'ESAs consult on technical standards for joint examination teams under DORA'; EBA press release on the first CTPP designation (18/11/2025)
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: footprint banks indirectly — the escalation endpoint of CTPP oversight is an ORDER TO THE BANK to suspend or terminate use of a non-compliant provider. That is an existential concentration risk for any bank whose customer channels run on a single hyperscaler. (b) BUY/CHANGE: strongest available argument for hybrid/on-prem or vendor-diversified delivery of ATM channel software (x-core multivendor), device telemetry, POS terminal management, and for keeping cryptographic key material in bank-controlled Thales HSMs rather than with a designated CTPP. Also drives demand for tested, evidenced exit strategies for every critical ICT service — a services engagement in itself. (c) BUDGET: annual redesignation cycle means the second CTPP list lands around Q4-2026; concentration-risk and exit-plan work should be in the 2027 IT plan set in Q4-2026.
signals.likelihood: High — oversight machinery is operational
signals.followup: Obtain the ESAs' final RTS on JET composition and the second annual CTPP designation list when published (expected around Q4-2026). Prepare a Printec 'exit strategy and substitutability' template for ATM/POS channel services as a sales asset.

signals.entity: Republic of Austria — NISG 2026 (NIS2 transposition)
signals.signal: [NEW — hard deadline inside 12 months] Austria's Netz- und Informationssystemsicherheitsgesetz 2026 (NISG 2026) transposing Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2) was passed by the Nationalrat on 12/12/2025 with the two-thirds majority needed for its constitutional provisions, cleared the Bundesrat on 18/12/2025, and was promulgated as BGBl. I Nr. 94/2025. It creates a federal Cybersecurity Office (Bundesamt fuer Cybersicherheit), a national cybersecurity strategy and a single point of contact. The act ENTERS INTO FORCE ON 01/10/2026 (nine months after publication in the Bundesgesetzblatt, on the first day of the following month). Affected essential and important entities must REGISTER WITHIN THREE MONTHS of entry into force — i.e. by 31/12/2026 — and must submit a mandatory SELF-DECLARATION (Selbsterklaerung) within twelve months of registration. Incident reporting is staged: early warning without delay and at the latest within 24 HOURS, full notification within 72 HOURS, final or progress report within ONE MONTH. Penalties: essential entities up to EUR 10 million or 2% of total worldwide prior-year turnover, whichever is higher; important entities up to EUR 7 million or 1.4%. Banking and financial market infrastructure are among the 18 covered sectors; press estimates put the population at roughly 4,000-5,000 Austrian organisations.
signals.source_name: Parlament Oesterreich, Gegenstand XXVIII/I/308 'Netz- und Informationssystemsicherheitsgesetz; Telekommunikationsgesetz, Gesundheitstelematikgesetz, Aenderung' (BGBl. I Nr. 94/2025, Nationalrat 12/12/2025, Bundesrat 18/12/2025); Schoenherr 'Oesterreich: NISG 2026 — Alles, was Sie wissen muessen' [Austria: NISG 2026 — everything you need to know] for the deadline and penalty detail
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: Austrian banks and financial market infrastructure — Erste Group, RBI, BAWAG, UniCredit Bank Austria, the Volksbanken and Raiffeisen sectors — plus their ICT suppliers. Financial entities are already under DORA (FMA/OeNB), so the practical incremental bite is registration, the self-declaration, management-body accountability and SUPPLY-CHAIN SECURITY duties, which reach non-financial ICT vendors that DORA touches only through contract. Critically, Erste and RBI export group ICT and vendor standards to subsidiaries across CZ, SK, HU, RO, HR, RS, BA, AL, ME, XK — so an Austrian rule sets the regional procurement bar. (b) BUY/CHANGE: a 24-hour early-warning clock plus a signed self-declaration on control effectiveness needs automated detection and retained evidence across the channel estate — Printec ATM/device telemetry and monitoring, INETCO transaction monitoring, 24x7 managed-service NOC. Supply-chain duties require vendor attestations and subcontractor disclosure (same pack as DORA Art.30 / RTS 2025/532). Asset-inventory and patching duties again surface end-of-life ATM/self-service platforms, feeding NCR Atleos refresh, x-core multivendor ATM software and Thales HSM/remote key injection. (c) BUDGET: entry into force 01/10/2026 and registration by 31/12/2026 means Austrian groups are scoping NOW; remediation capex sits in the 2027 plan agreed Q4-2026. This stacks on top of the ECB SSM-2026-0301 action plan due 31/10/2026 — the same Austrian CISO teams face both in the same quarter.
signals.likelihood: Certain — promulgated law with statutory dates
signals.followup: Confirm the exact BGBl publication date for BGBl. I Nr. 94/2025 on ris.bka.gv.at and check whether NISG 2026 expressly disapplies its security/reporting duties to DORA-regulated financial entities (lex specialis) — if it does, the value shifts to Printec's own compliance posture as a supplier. Time an Austrian campaign for Sept-Nov 2026 combining NISG registration and the ECB AI-threat action plan.

signals.entity: National Bank of Serbia (NBS) — ICT regulations for financial institutions
signals.signal: [VERIFIES AND CORRECTS the press-sourced Serbia row] The NBS's own register of regulations on supervision of financial institutions' information systems shows the operative framework is: (1) Odluka o minimalnim standardima upravljanja informaciono-komunikacionim sistemom finansijske institucije [Decision on minimum standards for managing the ICT system of a financial institution], Sluzbeni glasnik RS br. 102/2024 — this REPLACED the long-standing 2013 decision (Sl. glasnik RS 23/2013) and is the Serbian analogue of DORA's ICT risk-management pillar; (2) Odluka o uslovima i nacinu poveravanja aktivnosti u vezi sa informacionim sistemom finansijske institucije trecim licima [Decision on conditions and manner of outsourcing information-system activities to third parties], Sl. glasnik RS br. 100/2023 — the Serbian ICT third-party/outsourcing rule; (3) Odluka o tehnickim standardima za pouzdanu autentifikaciju korisnika i zajednickim i bezbednim otvorenim standardima komunikacije [Decision on technical standards for strong customer authentication and common secure open communication standards], Sl. glasnik RS br. 102/2024 (Serbia's SCA/RTS analogue); (4) Odluka o uslovima upravljanja informaciono-komunikacionim sistemom pruzaoca usluga povezanih s virtuelnim valutama, Sl. glasnik RS br. 49/2021. The identity-verification decision was AMENDED in 2026 (Sl. glasnik RS br. 43/2026). NBS has NOT published a DORA-titled decision — Serbia's DORA-equivalence is delivered through the 102/2024 + 100/2023 pair plus the Law on Information Security (Sl. glasnik RS 91/2025, in force 31/10/2025) transposing NIS2, whose implementing regulations are due by 31/10/2026.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Serbia — 'Propisi iz oblasti supervizije informacionih sistema finansijskih institucija' [Regulations on supervision of financial institutions' information systems] (official regulation register)
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: all Serbian banks — including Printec reference customers Raiffeisen Banka Srbija (x-core) and AIK Banka (NCR recyclers) — plus payment institutions, e-money institutions and virtual-asset service providers. (b) BUY/CHANGE: the 100/2023 outsourcing decision governs exactly what Printec sells as managed services — it requires the bank to document, risk-assess and supervise every third party touching its information system, with NBS notification and audit rights. Printec must supply a Serbian-law outsourcing pack (risk assessment inputs, audit-rights clause, exit plan, subcontractor list) as tender collateral. The 102/2024 minimum ICT standards drive asset inventory, logging, segmentation and change control across ATM/POS estates: telemetry and monitoring, x-core multivendor ATM software, TMS, Thales HSM and remote key injection, INETCO transaction monitoring on the new SEPA SCT rails (operational 05/05/2026). (c) BUDGET: no single hard Serbian date; the forcing events are the 31/10/2026 NIS2 implementing regulations and the Serbian banks' group parents (Raiffeisen/Erste/OTP/UniCredit/NLB) pushing DORA-grade standards down from Vienna/Budapest/Ljubljana. Budget with the 2027 IT plan set in Q4-2026.
signals.likelihood: Certain for the regulations; Medium for the timing of the NIS2 implementing acts
signals.followup: Open the full text of Sl. glasnik RS 102/2024 and 100/2023 to extract the incident-notification deadlines and the outsourcing notification thresholds, and build a Serbian-law annex. Check nbs.rs 'Nacrti' (drafts) periodically for any DORA-titled draft decision as Chapter 9 accession screening advances.

signals.entity: NBRNM (North Macedonia), FBA/ABRS (Bosnia & Herzegovina), BQK (Kosovo) — no DORA mirror yet
signals.signal: [STANDING — dated 2017-2020, with a live gap] Unlike Albania (DORA-mirror regulation adopted 01/07/2026) and Montenegro (Zakon o digitalnoj operativnoj otpornosti finansijskog sektora, Sl. list CG 14/26, dormant until EU accession), three footprint markets still supervise bank ICT under pre-DORA, pre-NIS2 rules: NORTH MACEDONIA — Odluka za Metodologijata za sigurnost na informativniot sistem na bankata [Decision on the Methodology for the security of a bank's information system], Sluzben vesnik br. 78/18 (2018), issued by NBRNM; BOSNIA & HERZEGOVINA — the Banking Agency of the Federation of BiH (FBA) applies the Odluka o upravljanju informacionim sistemom u banci [Decision on information system management in a bank], adopted 13/10/2017, Sluzbene novine FBiH br. 81/17, alongside a separate Odluka o upravljanju eksternalizacijom u banci [Decision on managing outsourcing in a bank], with the Banking Agency of Republika Srpska (ABRS) running a parallel entity-level regime and the CBBH holding no direct bank-supervision mandate; KOSOVO — BQK's Rregullore per Teknologji te Informacionit per Banka [Regulation on Information Technology for Banks], March 2020, which sets board responsibility for approving IT and security policies with an annual adequacy review. None of the three imposes DORA's four-hour major-incident clock, a register of information at subcontract level, or three-yearly threat-led penetration testing. All three are, however, on the same EU-accession path that produced the Albanian and Montenegrin texts, and all three are in the second Western Balkans TIPS-clone onboarding window expected November 2026.
signals.source_name: NBRNM — Odluka za Metodologijata za sigurnost na informativniot sistem na bankata (Sluzben vesnik 78/18); FBA — Odluka o upravljanju informacionim sistemima u bankama (Sl. novine FBiH 81/17) and Odluka o upravljanju eksternalizacijom u banci; BQK — Rregullore per Teknologji te Informacionit per Banka (March 2020)
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: banks in MK (Komercijalna, Stopanska, NLB, Halkbank, ProCredit), BA (UniCredit/Intesa/Raiffeisen/NLB/ASA/Addiko entities under FBA and ABRS) and XK (ProCredit, Raiffeisen, NLB, TEB, BKT, Banka Ekonomike). (b) BUY/CHANGE: the near-term driver in these three is NOT local regulation but (i) GROUP MANDATE — Raiffeisen, UniCredit, Intesa, NLB, OTP and Erste push DORA-grade ICT risk, incident and third-party standards from their EU parents into non-EU subsidiaries, and (ii) the TIPS-clone instant-payments go-live, which adds a 24x7 real-time rail that must be monitored. Sell INETCO transaction monitoring and ATM/device telemetry against the group standard rather than against a local rule, and position DORA-ready contract terms as future-proofing. The FBiH outsourcing decision is the concrete local hook for managed-services contracting in BA. (c) BUDGET: no local deadline to anchor on; anchor on the November 2026 TIPS-clone onboarding window for AL/XK/MK and on group 2027 IT plans set in Q4-2026.
signals.likelihood: Medium — a DORA mirror in MK/BA/XK is likely within the accession cycle but no draft is public
signals.followup: Set a watch on NBRNM's 'Odluki od oblasta na informatickata tehnologija' page, FBA/ABRS podzakonski akti and BQK's korniza ligjore for a DORA-titled draft — Albania moved from nothing to an adopted regulation in one cycle.
